answer: A farm running 99 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation low-cost. Because the wharf stake is held until the summit settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the kernel audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 45% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer burns proportionally more than endorsing a trivial one. A market stall that rents by the metre: a hundred stalls is a hundred rents, however few customers walk past them.
